text:
alex: Quick context — found a regression in the EU1 auth token refresh that spikes 502s for embedding requests around 12:20z. I prepared a minimal hotfix (auth-refresh-fallback) and need expedited approvals to push during the short change window at 12:45–13:00z. @maria @sam please advise.

maria: thanks for the heads-up. can you paste a 2-line release note and the exact deploy command? also what’s the rollback plan?

alex: release note: "Fix: fallback to legacy token refresh endpoint to prevent 502s for embeddings under heavy load (EU1)".

Deploy command (deploy-bot):
```
/deploy hotfix auth-refresh-fallback --env=prod --region=eu1 --canary=5% --notes="fallback for token refresh 502s"
```
rollback (manual):
```
/deploy promote previous:service:prod@v2.1.2 --region=eu1
```
Plan: 5% canary -> monitor 5m -> if green promote to 100% (30m backoff if any errors).

sam: quick Q — does this change any DB schema or config keys? i want a guaranteed no-migration note before approving. also tag me in the deploy ticket.

alex: no schema changes, pure runtime switch to alternate refresh URL with same auth headers. added unit+smoke tests. ticket: https://tickets/repo/INFR-4821 (linked in the deploy request). tagged @sam.

julie: what’s impact to SLOs if canary fails? should we preemptively pin traffic to dedicated capacity?

alex: if canary fails we’ll immediate rollback to v2.1.2 and shift EU1 requests to the reserved eu1 pool (manual route flip). SLO risk is <5min extra latency during rollback.

qa-bot: smoke tests for auth-refresh-fallback @ 12:32z: PASSED (basic token flow, embeddings sanity, retries). logs: `ok 18/18`.

maria: ok i can approve for expedited during the 12:45–13:00z window. sam need you to ack rollback plan or approve.

sam: acked, approve for expedite. i’ll be on-call for rollback actions. please include me in paging.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created by alex: ID #DPL-8772. Awaiting approvals: maria (approved), sam (approved). Canary target: 5% eu1. Scheduled: now (manual trigger).

alex: triggering now.

deploy-bot: Starting canary: hotfix auth-refresh-fallback -> eu1 (5%). Logs streaming: https://deploy/logs/DPL-8772/canary

deploy-bot: Canary health check (5m): 0 errors, latency within baseline, 502 rate reduced to normal. Marking canary green.

deploy-bot: Promoting to 100% in eu1.

julie: monitoring traces — looks good from SRE side. no elevated error budgets.

deploy-bot: Promotion complete. All instances running hotfix auth-refresh-fallback in eu1.

alex: release note pinned to changelog and sent to #release-notes. closing thread — thanks everyone. :rocket:
